title: Obex commits to publishing its default rates, not only its allocations and yields
content:
A.6.1.1.5.3.2.5 requires that "Obex maintains an active dashboard reporting total allocations, active projects, utilization, **default rates**, and realized yields."

Four of the five metrics are the ones any fund would volunteer. Default rates are the one that is normally omitted, deferred, or reported only in aggregate after enough time has passed to blur it — and its inclusion is what makes the rest interpretable. Realized yield without a default rate describes the survivors; utilization without defaults describes deployment without describing outcome.

The pairing with **utilization** is the more subtle one. For an Agent whose capital is borrowed as USDS debt against a Sky Allocation Vault, utilization is a leverage disclosure: it reveals how much of the available facility is drawn, which bears directly on the Encumbrance Ratio commitment Treadstone gave.

The commitment is also structurally weaker than the rest of the Artifact's controls. "Maintains an active dashboard" specifies no publication venue, no update frequency, no metric definitions, and no consequence for lapse — unlike the Freezer Multisig's reporting duty, which names the Sky Forum and a reasonable time frame. As drafted it is a standard Obex holds itself to rather than one anyone can enforce, and the definition of "default" for an early-stage project is exactly the kind of term a self-reporter benefits from leaving open.
description: The mandated dashboard covers total allocations, active projects, utilization, default rates and realized yields — putting the failure metric on the same footing as the performance metric.
